newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline weakens, Nigerians to buy cargoes.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline weakens, Nigerians to buy cargoes.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices weakened on Wednesday as the backwardation in the swaps market, generated by strong buying ahead of the UK budget next week, eased further.
Eurograde barges traded at $181 a tonne fob Antwerp for prompt/first half July material and dealers said a Scandinavian refiner was bidding for refinery barrels at $183 for the same period.

Arbitrage opportunities to the U.S. were still notionally unworkable. "It only takes the (NYMEX gasoline screen) to tick up by a couple of dollars more and people will get excited about this again," one dealer said.
Two or three cargoes have already been sold in the past week to transatlantic destinations to help clear Europe's surplus, but at prices which were out-of-the-money at the time.

A senior Nigerian official said his country would import 24 cargoes of gasoline from now until September to counter a scarcity of locally-produced gasoline. Most of this was thought likely to be sourced from the Med, where low octane material is currently in good supply. A refiner in the Med has already sold three cargoes this month to traders and these were expected to move to West Africa.

High octane material is still extremely tight in the Med and demand into Italy good. A refiner sold small a high octane cargo on Tuesday to an Italian buyer at an unusually large $4 over the high of published quotes. The exact grade and timing of the material was not known. -- London newsroom +44 171 542 8167
